text:
maya: Heads-up — noticed a new p99 TTFT bump on /v1/generate after the kernel-chooser change rolled last night. attaching profiler snapshot and a quick excerpt.
liam: thanks for flagging. is this across all model families or just the medium-sized ones? :thinking_face:
maya: mostly on the 13B variants. 7B looks stable. 70B too noisy to say yet.
alex: can you paste the top-level breakdown? a short table is fine.
maya: sure — from the perf trace (single-request sample):
```
TTFT: 126ms
kernel_exec: 88ms
prequeue_wait: 18ms
kvcache_fetch: 12ms
batching_overhead: 8ms
```
alex: kernel_exec is large but not unprecedented. what changed in selector? we switched to adaptive-latency mode, right?
jess: correct — selector now prioritizes kernel with best median latency for the last 5m window, which can favor kernels that misbehave on long-seq tails.
liam: that could explain p99 regressions even if p50 improved. median-based heuristics are blind to tails.
maya: yeah. i pulled a per-token timeline — spikes line up with kernel handoffs when kvcache misses increase for certain prefixes.
tom: can you share the profiler link? perf-bot should have an artifact.
perf-bot: profiler uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/profiler/1932109876/trace-1.tar.gz :white_check_mark:
maya: link above. i also dumped a short flame for the heavy sample — kernel switch occurs at token 5 and token execution jumps ~2x for tokens 6-8.
sam: curious if batching heuristics are interacting here — are we coalescing small sequences into a kernel that expects long sequences and paying penalty?
jess: good point. selector also toggles batch packer to favor full-AI pack for throughput when kernel median < 40ms; might create packing patterns that stress kvfetch.
liam: proposal: change selector scoring to use p95 weighted by sequence-length bucket. that should prefer safer kernels for long tails.
alex: let's validate by simulating with today's traffic replay. maya — can you run a replay with selector p95-weighted and post aggregated token-level breakdown? expect p50 similar, p99 less noisy.
maya: starting replay now, will post a short dashboard snapshot. ETA ~12m.
infra-bot: replay job 1932109876-r1 queued on ded-012 (g4dn). logs: https://ci.redwood/replay/1932109876-r1
maya: quick interim note: enabling aggressive kvcache-prefetch on the 13B path reduced kv_fetch from 12ms -> 2ms in a micro-run, but that increased memory pressure on ded nodes.
sam: hmm memory tradeoff could be viable on Dedicated but not for Hosted. maybe make prefetch an opt-in route-level config.
jess: agree. also add a dashboard per-route SLI mapping: TTFT -> kernel_exec, queue, kv_fetch, batch_wait. then expose p50/p95/p99 per SLI.
liam: I'm going to sketch the dashboard panel names and thresholds. share in #eng-dashboard and i'll pick it up.
maya: posted the replay results and the token-slice CSV in the perf artifacts. verdict: p99 drops ~28% with p95-weighted selector and kv-prefetch enabled for /v1/generate. full writeup incoming.
alex: awesome. once we have the writeup, let's run a canary with the new selector on 10% traffic and monitor token-level KPIs for 6h.
sam: agreed. add automated rollback trigger if route p99 TTFT increases by >5% for 10m.
maya: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
